Benthic index (TBBI) outcome by bay segment and year

Source: R/anlz_sed_tbbi.R
anlz_sed_tbbi.Rd

Benthic index (TBBI) outcome by bay segment and year

Usage

anlz_sed_tbbi(benthicdata)

Arguments

benthicdata

raw benthic monitoring data, e.g. tbeptools::benthicdata

Value

A data.frame with columns yr, bay_segment, TBBI (median station-level score for that bay segment/year), and outcome (0-1, 1 = best)

Details

Uses anlz_tbbiscr to get station-level TBBI scores (0-100), filtered to the same stations anlz_tbbimed uses for its bay segment grades (FundingProject == "TBEP", ProgramID == 4, and TBBI between 0 and 100, for the 7 bay segments anlz_tbbimed scores), then takes the median station score for each bay segment/year. outcome comes directly from that continuous median via util_outcome (type = "continuous", from = c(73, 87)), TBBI's own grade breakpoints (Degraded below 73, Intermediate 73-87, Healthy above 87). This is the same clamped-breakpoint-window treatment used for the Nekton Index's from = c(32, 46).

This bypasses anlz_tbbimed entirely, which instead grades a bay segment/year Poor/Fair/Good from the proportion of its stations falling in each of the Degraded/Intermediate/Healthy categories. This is a compound rule on those proportions, not a discretized version of a single continuous statistic, so there's no direct continuous equivalent of it the way there is for TBNI's or PEL/TEL's breakpoints. Scoring the median of the raw station values instead is a related but distinct measure. It can disagree with anlz_tbbimed's category in some edge cases (e.g. a bay segment split between many Healthy and a few very Degraded stations can have a middling median while still tripping the proportion rule's Degraded >= 0.2 condition for "Poor").

Examples

anlz_sed_tbbi(tbeptools::benthicdata)
#> # A tibble: 222 × 4
#>       yr bay_segment  TBBI outcome
#>    <dbl> <chr>       <dbl>   <dbl>
#>  1  1995 BCB          87.1   1    
#>  2  1996 BCB          84.1   0.793
#>  3  1997 BCB          78.2   0.368
#>  4  1998 BCB          83.6   0.755
#>  5  1999 BCB          80.3   0.523
#>  6  2000 BCB          85.4   0.885
#>  7  2001 BCB          80.3   0.522
#>  8  2002 BCB          78.7   0.406
#>  9  2003 BCB          84.4   0.811
#> 10  2004 BCB          85.3   0.879
#> # ℹ 212 more rows
